sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *aun cuando* from B2 Unit 8, the more formal sibling of *aunque*: the indicative for a fact (*Aun cuando tenía miedo, habló*), the subjunctive for a possibility or a point you grant (*Aun cuando sea difícil, hay que decir la verdad*). The Amazon gives many chances to use it, because protecting the forest is never easy.

sections.title: Aun cuando: fact or possibility
rows: Aun cuando haya problemas, hay que proteger la selva.
A possibility: subjunctive (*haya*). Even if there are problems...
Aun cuando el parque está cerrado a los turistas, muchas personas conocen sus pinturas.
A fact: indicative (*está*). Even though the park is closed...
Seguiremos protegiendo la selva aun cuando sea difícil.
A possibility after a future: subjunctive (*sea*).
Aunque sea difícil, hay que proteger la selva.

items.spanish: Aun cuando haya problemas, hay que proteger la selva.
items.english: Even if there are problems, the forest must be protected.

items.spanish: Aun cuando el parque está cerrado a los turistas, muchas personas conocen sus pinturas.
items.english: Even though the park is closed to tourists, many people know its paintings.

items.spanish: Seguiremos protegiendo la selva aun cuando sea difícil.
items.english: We will keep protecting the forest even if it is difficult.

items.spanish: Aun cuando llueva, los científicos entrarán en la selva.
items.english: Even if it rains, the scientists will go into the forest.

sections.content: Ask yourself whether the speaker presents the obstacle as a real fact (indicative) or as something possible that will not change the plan (subjunctive). *Aun cuando* is more formal than *aunque*; write *aun* without an accent here, because *aún* means "still".
